scenarios.name: evening_peak_full_battery
scenarios.rationale: Peak price, high load, nearly full battery: textbook hard discharge to shave peak.

scenarios.name: midday_pv_surplus_low_soc
scenarios.rationale: Large PV surplus, cheap grid, empty-ish battery: store the surplus.

scenarios.name: peak_price_empty_battery_soc_guard
scenarios.rationale: Price screams discharge but SOC is below the 10% floor. The correct move is hold. This is the key SOC-guard test.

scenarios.name: overnight_cheap_charge_window

state.price_context: off-peak overnight (lowest tariff of the day)

scenarios.rationale: Cheapest tariff, low SOC, morning ramp ahead: charge from grid.

scenarios.name: pv_surplus_battery_full_soc_guard
scenarios.rationale: PV surplus suggests charging but battery is above the 95% ceiling. Mirror image of scenario 3.

scenarios.name: shoulder_hour_no_signal
scenarios.rationale: No strong price or PV signal, balanced load: do nothing. Tests restraint - LLMs tend to over-act.

scenarios.name: high_price_mid_soc

state.price_context: peak pricing window (16:00-21:00), 4 peak hours remain

scenarios.rationale: Peak price with only half a battery and hours of peak left: discharge, with soft arguably smarter (ration across remaining peak hours).

scenarios.name: pre_peak_ramp_onset
scenarios.rationale: One hour before peak, battery nearly full: conserve for the peak (hold) or start easing in (soft). Hard discharge now wastes capacity.

scenarios.name: cheap_price_battery_full

state.price_context: off-peak overnight (lowest tariff of the day)

scenarios.rationale: Cheap price tempts charging but battery is above the ceiling; nothing to discharge for either.

scenarios.name: conflicting_signals_pv_and_peak
scenarios.rationale: PV surplus says charge, peak price says discharge. Any answer except charging at peak price is defensible - this probes the model's reasoning under conflict. Watch the reasoning field closely here.
